messages:
jon: Heads-up: Legal asked whether spans that contain PII (email/phone) are encrypted before export or redacted. Need a short plan for Dedicated + Private customers.

maria: We currently use an otel-collector attributes processor to drop a handful of well-known keys (user.email, user.phone). But teams keep adding ad-hoc attrs so coverage is inconsistent.

alex: Hashing vs encryption tradeoffs:
- deterministic hash preserves joinability but still considered PII by legal in some regions
- envelope encryption with per-tenant KEK + KMS gives audit trail but needs key rotation and adds latency

kevin: SRE concerns: hashed email still increases cardinality in our traces/indices. Tokenization with a central token service avoids cardinality but requires lookup for debugging.

maria: Lisa requested ability to produce an audit log of who decrypted raw values. KMS + access logging seems necessary for that requirement.

alex: Proposed short-term approach:
1) Add a 'sensitive_attrs' discovery sampler that collects candidate attr keys from production (only attribute names, no values).
2) Console UX for owners to mark attrs as 'sensitive' per service/version.
3) Otel-collector processor pipeline: mask (regex) => if marked sensitive then call crypto sidecar (envelope encrypt) => export. Fallback: strip if crypto unavailable.

Example otel-collector snippet we'd use as a jump-start:
```yaml
processors:
  attributes/sanitize:
    actions:
      - action: delete
        key: user.password
  attributes/mask_candidates:
    actions:
      - action: key_to_lower
        key: ""

exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: "ingest.redwood.internal:4317"
    tls:
      insecure: false

extensions:
  health_check: {}

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [attributes/sanitize, attributes/mask_candidates]
      exporters: [otlp]
```

jon: Can we avoid a full sidecar? Maybe add a grpc interceptor in our otlp exporter that calls KMS or a lightweight crypto API. That reduces deployment complexity for Private.

kevin: Perf note: per-span encryption is CPU-heavy. Need async batching + local cache of encrypted tokens for repeated values. Also ensure pipeline won't backpressure if KMS slow — strip & emit metric + alert.

lisa-legal: For compliance: we need (a) auditable decrypt events, (b) retention policy (raw must be deletable on request), (c) ability to export raw under approved legal workflows. Encryption + KMS + audit logs satisfies (a) and (b) if we can delete rekeyed copies.

privacy-bot: Automated scan: 12 services emitted 'user.email' attr in last 7d. See https://console.internal/redwood/privacy-scans

maria: Next steps: Alex/Kevin/Maria to draft RFC + prototype otel-collector config that supports pluggable crypto adapter. UX folks will mock Console flow for 'sensitive attr candidates'. Target: RFC by EOW.

jon: +1. Please include fallback modes (strip/encrypt/hash) in RFC and perf estimate. :thumbsup:
